blocks.x: In over three years at Collider, senior author Jake has now penned over 3000 articles covering a wide range of TV and film for the resources, lists, utilities, news, and interview teams. Alongside interviewing stars such as Selin Hizli, Rose Ayling-Ellis, Harlan Coben, and Chelsea Peretti, Jake was lucky enough to visit the set of Aardman and Netflix's Wallace and Gromit: A Vengeance Most Fowl in 2024, getting the chance to chat with four-time Academy Award winner Nick Park and Merlin Crossingham. Jake has also worked for other publications, including Agents of Fandom. You can also hear Jake every week as the resident film and TV journalist on Track Radio.

Ten months into 2026, the world has already lost several Hollywood icons. From Dolly Parton to Tim Curry, some of the best screen stars have sadly died this year. In July, the news broke that the iconic Sam Neill had passed away at the age of 78. According to a statement, Neill's passing was "sudden and unexpected," but he "passed with the dignity that has characterised his whole life."

From this moment, and to this day, fans across the world have honored Neill by diving into his impressive, vast catalog of projects. This includes his breakthrough in Sleeping Dogs, and the likes of My Brilliant Career, The Final Conflict, Possession, Dead Calm, The Hunt for Red October, and The Piano, to name just a few. But, of course, Neill's most famous film came in 1993, as he starred in Steven Spielberg's dino-sized blockbuster, Jurassic Park. As paleontologist Dr. Alan Grant, Neill shines as the man invited to evaluate the safety of the titular park.

He is joined by a stacked cast in the iconic '90s blockbuster, including Laura Dern as Ellie Sattler, Richard Attenborough as John Hammond, Bob Peck as Robert Muldoon, and Jeff Goldblum as Ian Malcolm. The film was an enormous hit both critically and commercially, scoring a box office haul of almost $1 billion, a milestone it finally crossed when it was re-released in 3-D in 2013. The movie won three Academy Awards, including Best Sound, Best Sound Effects Editing, and Best Visual Effects. 33 years later, you can continue your celebration of Neill by watching Jurassic Park at its new home on Starz.

Nobody is brave about this one.

AThe same thing I have watched a hundred times.
BSomething long, slow and beautiful.
CSomething big and loud with a great score.
DOne clever episode of something hopeful.

How deep do you go into something you love?

AI know every character and all the gossip.
BI have read the appendices and studied the maps.

DI want to know how the world actually works.

What do you and your friends actually argue about?

AWhich one of us is which type.
BWhether the adaptation got it right.
CWhether the new stuff ruined the old stuff.
DWhether the right thing was actually done.

How do you feel about a room full of strangers?
Every one of these comes with a very big room.

AGreat, and I will know everybody by the end.
BFine, as long as they take it seriously.
CBrilliant, especially if there is something to dress up for.
DHappy, provided the conversation is interesting.

Where would you rather spend a week?
Pick on instinct rather than on budget.

AAn old castle somewhere rainy.
BMountains, long walks, no phone signal.
CA desert with an unbelievable night sky.
DA city built around a university.

What do you believe about people, mostly?
All four of these stories have an answer, and they disagree.

AMost of them turn out better than expected.
BThe smallest ones decide the biggest things.
CAnybody can change, even very late on.
DWe work it out if we keep talking.

AEverything I owned when I was twelve.
BHardbacks, in order, read more than once.
CFigures, posters, and a few things still boxed.
DBooks about how things work, plus a model or two.

Starfleet Academy brought the franchise back to a classroom in 2026, which is
appropriate, because Trek has always been a bit of a seminar.

You would want the conversation afterwards more than the episode itself, and here you
will always find somebody willing to have it.
